strengths: The Reroll is one job on the primary GM: every refusal is asked before anything is paid, including that the message still holds the dice the GMs kept (reroll.mjs:484-534, standingRolls 550-556), and a journal row with phases says how far a cut Reroll got, so a reload is given back or told rather than paid twice (reroll.mjs:591-631, 793-807, 946-982).

What a roller may say about a roll is a closed, typed list per action (action-pipeline.mjs:531-564, ROLL_CLAIMS and CLAIM_AS); a GM's fact is written only on the row of the roll its packet names, for that sender, character and action, and parked until the row exists (noteFactOfRoll 786-802, takeFactsAwaiting 768-778).

A Listen's Reroll is heard on the roller's own browser from the GM's bare entry (reroll.mjs:1877-1926, heardLines), so the GM's knowledge of an unfound death cannot reach the roller through the new lines.

Every action pays before its dice and gives an honest cancel back with the receipt that paid (a Burst comes back as a Burst), and a later roll's cancel after one has landed keeps the price (action-pipeline.mjs:975-990; used in action-doors.mjs:145-147, action-tail.mjs:244-247).
The phase is asked of one table for the press and the tile (allowed-now.mjs:48-116, read once in action-rolls.mjs:136-137 and 208); a `free` action is a GM's alone (action-rolls.mjs:101).

A Search takes the room's token only once the dice are on the table, refuses a 'something specific' with no GM before the price and again before the token, and tells a sealed room from an empty one (action-search.mjs:99-141, 504-576).

The briefing's numbers are read from the tables the roll is scored against, for this character as they stand (tool relief, watchers through the same filter the roll uses): action-briefing.mjs:203-217, 254-326, 335-354.

The rules manager writes once per save, reads the write's answer before saying 'Saved', refuses an emptied rule with a message and announces introduced and revoked rules by default (rules.mjs:560-603).

Each Infiltrate replay names what it cannot take back and says so in the roller's lines (infiltrate-reroll.mjs:12-16 and each settle*), and a pick's replay tells no room and leaves no second trace (doors-gm.mjs:228-237 with `tell: false`).

findings.title: A GM playing a student through the Infiltrate rows is told the wrong result: the GM's own client gets the handler's whole answer, `{ reply: {...} }`, and the rows read the fields off its top
findings.where: scripts/bridge-guards.mjs:1947-1948 (a GM's `local` settles with the handler's raw answer) against 1819 (a player is sent `out.reply`); scripts/bridge-runs-acts.mjs:188, 204 and the returns of handleEchoes, handleWatchDeclare, handleDoorForce, handleDoorPick, handleEavesdrop, handleTailStart (`return { reply: {...} }` or `{ refused }`); readers scripts/action-listen.mjs:278, 290-291, 323-325, 355-358; scripts/action-doors.mjs:41-44, 91-96, 152-157; scripts/action-watch.mjs:205-208; scripts/action-tail.mjs:255-258
findings.what_happens: bridge-asks.mjs gives each E69/E74 ask a `local` closure that calls the bridge handler itself on a GM's client, and the waiter settles `{ ok: true, value }` with whatever the handler returned. The handlers return `{ reply: { moves } }`, `{ reply: { room, steps } }`, `{ reply: { forced, held } }` and so on - the shape the judge unwraps for a player (`answer(decl, ctx, out?.reply ...)`). The player's half then reads `res.value?.moves`, `?.room`, `?.forced`, `?.opened`, `?.kept`, `?.seen`, `?.moved`, which on a GM's own client are all undefined. So for a GM running a student: a Dash says 'Dash: 0 free crossings' whatever it granted; Echoes says 'you hear nobody'; Shut the Door says 'You barricade .' with no room; Force the Door and Pick the Lock say 'Nothing holds the door' even when it gave way or the lock opened; Keep Watch says 'You cannot settle into a watch this time' when the watch is kept; a tail that was noticed is reported as unnoticed; Listen's eavesdrop line never shows. A refusal (`{ refused }`) is read as success by Dash and Echoes (the same wrong lines, the action kept spent) and is silent in the other rows, where the bridge would have told a player why.
findings.failure_scenario: The GM, playing an NPC student from its sheet, forces a barricaded door with a 19; the door gives way on the map, and the GM's card reads 'Nothing holds the door to Library'.
findings.expected: One answer shape on both roads: the GM's own run read as a player's is (the `reply`), and a `{ refused }` said as the bridge says it to a player.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for an unwrap between the handler and the reader: `ask` (bridge-table.mjs:1653-1661) passes `local` through to bridgeRequest unchanged, and createWaiter's local branch (1947-1952) settles the raw value; no `local` closure in bridge-asks.mjs:55-150 maps `.reply`. Looked for a test of a GM's own row: audit/harness/scenarios/33-bridge-paths.mjs E69-A (1932-1960) and the Shut and Echoes checks after it run on p1's page; tier 2's E74-T7 and E74-T11 drive the handlers and settleInfiltrate directly; tier 0 only reads the rows' sources for their `sayNotDone` literals (tests-tier0.mjs:10578-10584). None presses a row on a GM's client and reads the card. The world's state is right in every case (the handler ran); only the card and the returned value are wrong. Facilities (action-facilities.mjs:159) returns the same raw shape, but performRest returns it to nobody who reads it.
findings.tests_near: 33-bridge-paths E69-A (p1), tier 2 E74-T7, E74-T11; no result read (no base-run.json).

findings.title: A Reroll of Force the Door that did not force it runs the whole attempt again: a second Remnant for the one attempt, and the rooms told a second time
findings.where: scripts/infiltrate-reroll.mjs:83-96 (settleForce calls forceDoor with no way to keep it quiet); scripts/doors-gm.mjs:157-198 (forceDoor: tellRooms 179-191, leaveDoorTrace 195, no `tell` parameter) against pickLock 205-237 (`tell = true`, and the replay's `tell: false`)
findings.what_happens: settleForce, for a first throw that did not force the door, calls doors-gm.mjs `forceDoor` with the new total. forceDoor is the first throw's whole run: it tells the character's room (and, when loud, the room beyond and the rooms next to both) 'X tries to force the door' or 'X forces the door', and 'Every attempt leaves a Remnant' - so the replay leaves a second door trace beside the first throw's, which nothing retunes or removes. pickLock was given `tell` for exactly this ('a Reroll's replay, whose cover the two rooms were told of by the first throw'; 'a Reroll's replay leaves none of its own'); forceDoor was not.
findings.failure_scenario: A student fails to force a locked door with a 9, buys a Reroll and gets 11, still a miss: the classmate in the room gets 'Aiko tries to force the door to Library' twice, and the investigation later finds two Remnants of one attempt at that door.
findings.expected: As a pick's replay: the rooms and the trace of the first throw stand (or are retuned), and the replay neither tells nor leaves a trace of its own.
findings.refutation_tried: Read forceDoor whole for a guard on a repeat (a fact, a flag, a dedupe of the trace by roll): none; leaveDoorTrace (457) is called with no roll id. Looked for a test: E74-T11 drives settleInfiltrate for a pick only (tests-tier2.mjs:102310-102373); no test names settleForce or a forced door's Reroll (grep `settleInfiltrate` in the tiers and scenarios). A first throw that did force the door is not touched ('forceStands', 84-86).

findings.title: A Keep Watch rerolled drops the roll's Despair: the first throw's Sanity mark stays when the Reroll succeeds, and a Reroll into a miss with Despair costs none
findings.where: scripts/infiltrate-reroll.mjs:26 and 33 (withHope computed, not passed to settleWatch), 127-137; scripts/watch-gm.mjs:60, 69-75 (`withHope = true` by default; a miss with Despair writes a Sanity mark)
findings.what_happens: settleInfiltrate reads `withHope` off the new roll and hands it to the Force and Pick replays, but calls `settleWatch(actor, total, isCritical, done)` without it, and settleWatch calls `declareWatch({ actor, total, isCritical })`, whose `withHope` defaults to true. So the replay never charges the miss-with-Despair Sanity mark, and nothing gives back the mark the first throw charged. The file's header says everything but the named exceptions is 'replaced', 'a watch kept or let go' among them.
findings.failure_scenario: A student misses Keep Watch with Despair and takes a Sanity mark, buys a Reroll and keeps the watch with a 15: the watch is kept and the mark the miss cost stays on the sheet.
findings.expected: The replay judged on the new roll's duality, as the first throw was, and what the first throw's result cost given back where the result no longer stands - or the exception said in the header and the line.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for the mark being handled elsewhere: makeReroll's settleDualityReroll moves only Daggerheart's Hope/Sanity/Fear of the duality and skips a critical's Sanity (reroll.mjs:223-250); nothing in settleWatch or the Reroll's give-back touches stress. Whether the owner means a watch's Despair price to stand like a theft is not written in docs/dev/e74 as far as the header reads; if it is meant, this is a comment against code rather than a rule bug.
findings.tests_near: none for a watch's Reroll (E74-T7 and E74-T11 drive a Dash, a room action and a pick).

findings.title: A Work on Project's Reroll gives back an action on the roller's own claim: `refunded` and `burst` are claims no GM fact holds, and a second roll.bookmark inside the minute rewrites them
findings.where: scripts/action-pipeline.mjs:534 (ROLL_CLAIMS.project: relief, bonus, refunded, burst) and 676-690 (the same roll again replaces its claims); scripts/reroll.mjs:1208, 2081-2100 (settleActionRefund reads both and writes on the GM); scripts/actions.mjs:243-254 (refundAction: a grant receipt gives a Burst); scripts/action-project.mjs:594-597 (the honest first throw's values)
findings.what_happens: The first throw's critical gives its action back on the roller's browser and tells the GMs `refunded: true` and `burst` (what paid). Since fix r2-H3 a Work's `relief` and `bonus` are held to what the GM sees (projectExtrasHeld), but `refunded` and `burst` are read raw: settleActionRefund compares the claimed `refunded` with the new roll's critical and refunds an action (or a Burst when `burst` says so) on the GM, with no look at the credit the GMs hold of that payment - the check the paid-back roads use (sheet-audit.mjs:1051-1062). guardRollAuthor lets the roller send roll.bookmark for the same message again for a minute (bridge-guards.mjs:1183), and keepGmBookmark replaces the row's claims with the new packet's (687-690). A console that resends `refunded: false` after a critical's refund, then buys a Reroll that lands a critical, gets a second action for one roll; `burst: true` on an action-paid Work turns a critical's refund into a Burst, which covers any one action whatever it costs (actions.mjs:166-177).
findings.failure_scenario: A player whose Work rolled a critical (action back) resends the roll's bookmark from the console with refunded false, spends 3 Hope on a Reroll and lands another critical: the GM's client hands the character a second action for the one roll.
findings.expected: Whether the first throw's action came back, and from what, read as a GM fact (the progress handler or the GMs' credit), as `progress`, `relief` and `bonus` are held since r2-H3.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a hold: projectExtrasHeld (action-project.mjs:694-699) holds relief and bonus only; claimedOn (reroll.mjs:374-379) gives the first throw's duality but settleActionRefund does not read it; refundAction on a GM writes through meansWrite with no credit check (actions.mjs:247-252), and grantFreeActions writes `reason: "refund"` as a GM's write. The comment at action-pipeline.mjs:510-517 accepts claims that touch only the roller's own sheet; this one lands as a GM's write of the roller's purse, which the audit does not judge. The gain needs a console write, 3 Hope and a critical (about 1 in 12), so it is minor. The same class as ROLL-02's open half (a Search's `claimed`, old-1.2.42-rolls.json), not that item.
findings.tests_near: none that sends roll.bookmark twice for a Work (30-security and 83-roll-integrity not read for it here).

findings.title: Four of the GM's writes a Reroll makes to a student's purse still read it off the document, not as the GMs hold it
findings.where: scripts/actions.mjs:267-280 (takeBackRefund: `freeActionsLeft(actor)`, `actionsLeft(actor)`), 134-144 (grantFreeActions / grantFreeMoves: the document's count + n), reached on the GM from reroll.mjs:2089-2097 and infiltrate-reroll.mjs:47; scripts/infiltrate-reroll.mjs:49-50 (a Dash's crossings taken down from `freeMovesLeft(actor)`); scripts/watch-gm.mjs:72-74 (declareWatch's Sanity mark from the document's stress, also on the replay)
findings.what_happens: E29 fix r2-H24 moved refundAction, setActions and resetActionsFor onto meansWrite, because on the primary a player's write the audit puts back stands on the document until the put-back lands, and a GM's write computed from it becomes the GMs' value (sheet-audit.mjs:1007-1016, 'READ WHEN WRITTEN'). takeBackRefund, the two grant writers and the Dash replay's take-down were left on the document's count, though every one of these keys is in the audit's LEDGER (sheet-audit.mjs:177-184), and each runs on the primary inside a Reroll. A console's raised action count or Burst counter that is still waiting for its put-back when a Reroll loses a Work's critical, or rerolls a Dash lower, is written back by the GM minus one and stands.
findings.failure_scenario: A player writes 5 actions onto their sheet from the console and at once buys a Reroll that loses a Work's critical: the primary's take-back writes 4 over the put-back pending on 5, and the student keeps two actions the table never gave.
findings.expected: Each GM write of a student's means read as the GMs hold it, in the student's audit queue (meansWrite / gmMeansWrite), as refundAction's is.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a census that would hold these: tier 1 R290 (tests-tier1.mjs:11220) reads only maxima inside a GM's job, and these roads are not jobs; the watch's write is listed in R1441's reserve census as 'a watch missed with Despair, its Sanity mark, written' (tests-tier1.mjs:47198), which names it without asking where its value is read. The window is the put-back's round trip, or for good where a put-back fails (sheet-audit.mjs:1013-1016); its length at a table is not measured.

findings.title: The Tamper menu's button says Roll on its Reshape and Body rows, which open a window of their own first
findings.where: scripts/action-tamper.mjs:45 (one `confirm` for every row), 130-134 (Body opens openMoveBodyDialog), 146-153 (Reshape opens askTransformChange before any roll); the rule in scripts/action-listen.mjs:75-78 (E100 item 6: a row that opens a window of its own says Next)

Cover and Frame roll from the press; Reshape asks the change in a second window and Body opens the move-the-body dialog. findings.refutation_tried: chooseVariant takes a per-row `confirm` (action-menus.mjs:211-215, followConfirmLabel 479-492); Tamper's rows set none. Whether the E100 rule was meant beyond the Infiltrate and Search windows is not written in the code read; R4105 is named for Infiltrate.

findings.title: Direct Murder reads promptForNote's answer as an object whatever the opening lists: with one statistic listed the killer's sentence would be lost
findings.where: scripts/action-murder.mjs:376-385; scripts/action-menus.mjs:513-537 (an object only when `traits` lists more than one, else a string)
findings.what_happens: performDirectMurder destructures `const { note, proposed } = await promptForNote(...)`. promptForNote answers `{ note, proposed }` only when the list has two or more statistics; otherwise it answers the sentence as a string, and destructuring a string gives `note` undefined, so the parked declaration would carry no sentence. Today MURDER_OPENING's killer lists body and hand (config.mjs ~3686), so the object road is the one taken; the other is latent until the table changes.
findings.failure_scenario: After a config change that lists only Body for the killer's opening, a killer types how they mean to kill and the GM's card at the lights shows no sentence.
findings.expected: One answer shape from promptForNote, or the caller reading both.
findings.refutation_tried: listedTraits (trait-ruling.mjs:137-141) reads the config's list, filtered to known statistics; config lists two, so nothing breaks on 1.2.118. performBetrayal calls promptForNote without traits and reads the string (action-murder.mjs:288-295), correctly.
